question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key Naval Battles in Indian Waters and the Victors]
options: Battle of Diu (1509) — Portuguese victory over Gujarat-Egyptian-Calicut fleet
Battle of Swally (1612) — English victory over Portuguese fleet
Battle of Colachel (1741) — Travancore Kingdom victory over the Dutch East India Company
Battle of Bidara (1759) — French victory over the British Royal Navy
wrong_fact: The Battle of Bidara (also known as the Battle of Chinsurah/Hooghly) in 1759 was a decisive British victory over the Dutch forces, not a French victory over the British Royal Navy.
explanation: The Battle of Diu (1509) established Portuguese hegemony. the Battle of Swally (1612) marked the beginning of Portuguese decline in India at the hands of the English. The Battle of Colachel (1741) was a famous victory where King Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated the Dutch VOC fleet. The Battle of Bidara (1759) saw Colonel Francis Forde defeat a Dutch-allied force in Bengal, cementing British supremacy and ending Dutch political ambitions in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Naval Bases/Ports and the European Power that Held Supremacy there (18th Century)]
options: Trincomalee — Captured by the British from the Dutch to dominate the Bay of Bengal
Pondicherry — French stronghold besieged and captured multiple times by the British Royal Navy
Goa — Portuguese headquarters which remained highly contested and was captured by the French in 1756
Calcutta (Fort William) — British base from which naval expeditions were launched to control the Hooghly river
wrong_fact: Goa was never captured by the French in 1756. It remained under Portuguese control continuously from 1510 until 1961, despite facing Dutch blockades and Maratha land campaigns.
explanation: Trincomalee was captured by the British in 1782 (and permanently in 1795) to secure naval control over the Bay of Bengal. Pondicherry was repeatedly captured by the British during the Carnatic and Seven Years' wars and later restored. Calcutta was the main British presidency base in Bengal. Goa, the capital of the Portuguese State of India, was never taken by the French; it stayed Portuguese until India's annexation in 1961.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Naval Commanders and their Crucial Theatres of Operation/Confrontations]
options: Admiral Watson — Joint operations with Robert Clive to recapture Calcutta and eliminate Gheriah (Maratha base)
Admiral Suffren — Brilliant French commander who fought a series of masterclass naval battles against Edward Hughes off the Coromandel coast
Cornelis de Houtman — Dutch commander who led the blockade of Lisbon in 1595 to force open the spice routes
Francisco de Almeida — First Portuguese Viceroy who established naval hegemony over the western coast of India
wrong_fact: Cornelis de Houtman was the merchant-explorer who led the first Dutch expedition (Eerste Schipvaart) to the East Indies (modern Indonesia) in 1595-1597 via the Cape of Good Hope, NOT a military commander blockading Lisbon.
explanation: Admiral Charles Watson commanded the British East Indies Station and worked closely with Clive to retake Calcutta (1757) and defeat the Maratha Admiral Kanhoji Angre's successors at Gheriah. Admiral Pierre André de Suffren fought the British fleet under Edward Hughes in a brilliant 1782-1783 Indian Ocean campaign. Francisco de Almeida laid the Portuguese naval foundation. Cornelis de Houtman opened up the spice route by sailing directly to Bantam, bypassing the Lisbon trade, not blockading it.
